questions.q: What problem do automatic receipts solve?
options: They eliminate the need for a remittance bank account
They let Receivables create receipts in bulk for eligible transactions instead of manual entry one at a time
They replace the need for receipt methods entirely
They convert standard receipts into miscellaneous receipts
questions.explain: Automatic receipts are designed for high-volume, recurring collection scenarios like direct debit, where manually entering every receipt wouldn't scale.

questions.q: Which of the following is required for a transaction to be eligible for automatic receipt creation?
options: The transaction must be in a foreign currency
The customer must have no credit limit
The receipt method's receipt class must have a creation method of Automatic
The transaction must be a miscellaneous receipt
questions.explain: Only transactions tied to a receipt method whose receipt class is configured for automatic creation are eligible for the batch.

questions.q: What does the 'lead days' setting control in an automatic receipts batch?
options: How many customers can be included in one batch
The number of approval signatures required
The currency conversion rate used
The allowed gap between the batch run date and the transaction's due date
questions.explain: Lead days define the window between the batch date and the due date within which a transaction is considered eligible for the batch.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'approve' step in the automatic receipts batch process?
options: It formats the file for the bank
It acts as a control point to review the batch before it becomes final
It automatically reverses any errors
It replaces the need to remit the batch to the bank
questions.explain: The approve step is a control checkpoint, letting someone review the batch before confirming and remitting it.

A list of customers who missed a dunning letter
A report of write-offs approved during the period
A group of confirmed receipts sent to the bank together in one submission
questions.explain: A remittance batch groups confirmed receipts, ordered by maturity date and amount, into a single submission to the bank.
